_about: The groomer garage (task 4.50 phase 5; owner 2026-11-24): a two-bay maintenance shop, the smallest garage, from the shared metal-panel builder (bldgkit/metal_building.py), a sibling of the pump house: the same 60 x 40 ft footprint and 4:12 gable along u, the same panel and colours, a 20 ft eave (the pump house's 16 ft plus room over the 16 ft doors). It is a service shop, not parking: groomers park outside (as at big resorts) and each bay serves one machine (a groomer, a truck) at a time, so the bays are the bottleneck for servicing. Two 24 x 40 ft bays from the -u end, each behind a 20 x 16 ft overhead door on the +v (yard) side; the last 12 ft at the +u end is the shop end (office and parts room): a man door with its hood and lights and a window on the yard side, a second man door and two windows on the +u gable beside the fuel pad. The -u bay doubles as the wash bay (a high louvre on its gable). Styled like the pump house (round 7, owner: "make both options match the style of the pump house"; round 2: the first, a 48 ft box with a 22 ft eave and a 2:12 roof, looked ugly beside it; the round 1-6 flair, amber doors, a MAINTENANCE board and a light band, is gone): dark doors, a row of small high windows along the back and on the wash-bay gable at the pump house's 3 x 2 ft and its distance under the eave (eye-level windows only in the shop end's office), its roof and ridge vents. Round 8: the owner chose this gable over a single-slope version (round 6). The fuel pad (bldgkit/fuel_pad.py, owner: a tank with a little dispenser) lies along the shop end, the tank 5 ft off the wall and the lane beyond it (round 3), its own part. Same frame and keys as pumphouse.json and booster.json; gable doors give `at` (along v) instead of `u`. `fit`: the machines that must pass the doors and fit a bay with `spare` all round (Gate 0: a 400/600-class groomer is 9.1 m long with blade and tiller, 4.6 m wide with the blade folded, 2.9 m tall and 3.55 m with the cab tilted; the maker's space per machine is 11 x 6 x 3.5 m).

fuel._about: the fuel pad along the shop end (+u gable), in its own frame (x along the tank, y toward the lane; bldgkit/fuel_pad.py), turned so the tank lies along the gable (owner round 3: as close to the building as is realistic, so a groomer can pull up): a 6,000 gal protected double-wall diesel tank (UL 2085 type, 8 ft x 16 ft 9 in; owner round 4: bigger, so 6,000 gal, the largest that keeps the 5 ft setback) on two saddles, 300 mm clear of the pad, 5 ft off the wall (the fire codes' least for a protected tank of 6,000 gal or less; 0 ft to its own dispenser); the dispenser on a curbed island just outboard of it; the fuelling lane past the island, wide enough for a groomer with its blade folded, which drives along the gable from the yard, fuels and drives on round the back; bollards at the tank's ends and the island's; a 5.5 m pole light reaching over the island. `machine` [length, width]: the machine in the lane, for the checks

fit._about: machines in mm [length, width, height]: the groomer with its blade folded and its cab tilted (the tallest it gets in a bay), a crew pickup; each must pass its door and fit a bay with `spare` on every side. `bayWidth`: a bay's width along u (the shop end takes the rest); `wall`: the panel wall's thickness inside the footprint. `openBlade`: the groomer's blade open, which only has to pass the door (it is folded inside). `tankGap`: the fuel tank's least distance to the wall (5 ft, a protected tank); `laneGap`: the fuelling machine's least distance to the wall.
